territorial_scope.description: Applies as Illinois state law to dissemination of private sexual images, as stated in the enacting clause.

evidence.quote: Be it enacted by the People of the State of Illinois, represented in the General Assembly:

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Amends Illinois's Civil Remedies for Nonconsensual Dissemination of Private Sexual Images Act to extend its definitions and liability exceptions to digitally altered sexual images, meaning synthetic media that falsely appear authentic. Takes effect upon becoming law.
summary.long: The bill amends Sections 5 and 15 of the Civil Remedies for Nonconsensual Dissemination of Private Sexual Images Act. It adds 'digitally altered sexual image' (visual media created or substantially altered so that it would falsely appear to a reasonable person to be an authentic depiction of an individual) and extends 'depicted individual' and 'sexual image' to cover such images. Section 15(a) applies the good-faith exceptions to dissemination or threatened dissemination of digitally altered sexual images. Section 15(d) provides that dissemination is not a matter of public concern solely because the image is accompanied by a political message. Existing exceptions, including for law enforcement, legal proceedings, medical purposes, reporting of unlawful or unwelcome conduct, and a parent's or guardian's disclosure of a child's intimate image, are retained. The document reproduces the sections before and after amendment by P.A. 103-294 (eff. 1-1-24); the digitally altered image provisions appear in the after-version. Section 99 provides that the Act takes effect upon becoming law. Civil liability provisions outside Sections 5 and 15 are not reproduced.

notes: The bill reproduces Sections 5 and 15 of 740 ILCS 190 in two versions, one before and one after P.A. 103-294. The text does not say which version becomes operative. Section 95 states that using text in effect does not accelerate or delay the changes made by this Act or provisions derived from other Public Acts. The 'after' versions add definitions of digitally altered sexual image and extend the sexual image and depicted individual definitions, and add a political-message clause to Sec. 15(d). Annotations cover operative text only as printed; no registry ID is given for the amended Act or P.A. 103-294.

thresholds.variable_text: Child: an unemancipated individual who is less than 18 years of age
thresholds.consequence: Defines 'child' for the Act; under Sec. 15(b), a parent, legal guardian or individual with legal custody of a child is not liable for dissemination of an intimate private sexual image of the child, subject to Sec. 15(c). The definition appears in both the pre- and post-P.A. 103-294 versions of Sec. 5(1).
thresholds.conditions: Individual must be unemancipated; the Sec. 15(b) exception does not apply where Sec. 15(c) applies.

evidence.quote: "Child" means an unemancipated individual who is less than 18 years of age.
